name: IEC mode dependency (M)
summary: Dependency label Mm used to show operating modes; affected inputs and outputs act only in the selected mode.
description: M dependency is used where a device has several operating modes. When an Mm input is at its internal 1 state, inputs and outputs labelled m have their normal effect; otherwise they are disabled. Mode inputs are often produced from two select lines by binary grouping, giving M0 to M3.

Universal shift registers and up/down counters are typical users. On the symbol, a label such as 1,4D means the input acts as data only in mode 1 and with control 4. Reading these compound labels from left to right gives the order of conditions.
The notation does not define what happens during a mode change. Any restrictions on changing mode while clocking are device-specific.
readingNotes: Decode the mode inputs before reading other labels.
Compound labels list affecting numbers separated by commas.
drawingChecklist: Show the mode-select inputs and their binary grouping.
Label affected terminals with the mode numbers.
Tabulate the modes in a note if the symbol is complex.
distinction: A (address) dependency selects among arrays of identical elements; M selects operating modes of one element.
